correction.text: Carinthia with the Carniolan march, as it stood until Henry III split Carniola off in 1040

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Carinthia row; its Holy Roman Empire shape draws the land as imperial). The duchy is Carinthia plus the Carniolan march, which Henry III 'split off' in 1040. The Carantanian march (later Styria) and the March of Verona were attached to it as marches (976 to 1180 and 976 to 1151) and are drawn as the vassal tint, not as direct land. The infobox area 10,327 km2 is the 1910 crown land (the gazetteer Kärnten alone is about 9,600 km2, ratio 0.93; with Carniola, about 19,200 km2 more, the shape is about 28,800 km2).

New keyframe: after Henry III cut the Carniolan march off in 1040 the direct duchy is Carinthia (infobox area 10,327 km2 for 1910; gazetteer about 9,600 km2). Dukes came from the Eppenstein (1012-1122), Sponheim and later houses; Habsburg from 1335. Whether the Carinthian duchy kept the Lavant valley and the Lower Carinthian (Slovenian) lands is not on the page.

region.text: Carinthia with the Carniolan march, as it stood until Henry III split Carniola off in 1040

ledger.note: 976: Otto II splits Carinthia from Bavaria and installs Henry the Younger as its first duke. 'It was separated from the Duchy of Bavaria in 976, and was the first newly created Imperial State' (infobox 'Created Duchy: 976'). The Carniolan march is read as part of the new duchy because the page has Henry III 'split off' Carniola in 1040.

region.text: the Carantanian march beyond the Koralpe to the Mur, Mürz and Enns

ledger.note: 976: the Carantanian march (later Styria) passes under the new duke. 'In 976, it was transferred to the jurisdiction of the newly created Duchy of Carinthia'; its territory comprised 'the adjacent eastern territory beyond the Koralpe range on to the Mur River, Mürz and Enns rivers'. It was known as the March of Styria from the middle of the 11th century.

region.text: the Veronese march with Trentino, Friuli and Istria

ledger.note: 976: Otto II gives the March of Verona to the duke of Carinthia. Otto II established the Duchy of Carinthia and 'He also received Verona as a Carinthian march'; the dukes of Bavaria had held both Carinthia and Verona in 952-975. The march's territory is the Verona page's, in part undated.

978: Henry the Younger loses Carinthia. He 'joined the failed War of the Three Henries and lost Carinthia two years later' (977-978); the page says Otto I succeeded him. He regained the ducal title in 985.

1012: Adalbero of Eppenstein is vested with the duchy; the Istrian march goes to Count Poppo of Weimar. Adalbero had become margrave of the Carinthian March c. 1000; the March of Styria page dates his enfeoffment 1011/12 and his deposition 1035.

1040: Henry III splits off the Carniolan march. 'Henry III split off the Carniolan march and granted it to Margrave Poppo' after inheriting Carinthia in 1039. [Reviewer eu-08-x, 2026-10-25: counterpart set to the slug march-of-carniola listed in the author's counterparts_needing_dossiers]
1077: Luitpold (Eppenstein) receives the duchy; the Eppenstein line ends with Henry III of Carinthia in 1122.
1122: the Eppenstein line dies out and Henry IV of the Sponheim house rules in 1122-1123. 'which, however, became extinct with the death of Luitpold's younger brother Henry III of Carinthia in 1122'.
1151: Conrad III takes the Veronese march from the duke of Carinthia. Conrad III 'divested Duke Henry V of Carinthia of the remaining Veronese march'; Herman III of Baden held it 1151-1160.
1180: Styria becomes a duchy of its own. 'In 1180, his son and successor Margrave Ottokar IV was finally elevated to the rank of Duke of Styria by Emperor Frederick Barbarossa.'

1335: Louis the Bavarian gives Carinthia to the Habsburgs. He 'gave Carinthia and the southern part of the Tyrol as an imperial fief to the Habsburg family on 2 May in Linz'; the Habsburg dukes of Austria took over (infobox 1335). The Treaty of Neuberg of 1379 later placed it in Inner Austria.

wars.name: War of the Three Henries
wars.outcome: Henry II of Bavaria revolted against Otto II in 974 and was deposed in 976; Otto II cut Carinthia out of Bavaria. Henry the Younger, the first duke of Carinthia, joined the failed war of 977-978 and lost Carinthia.

certainty.note: No treaty draws the Carinthian frontier on the pages opened; the Habsburg grant of 1335 is a feudal investiture.

notes: Three pages opened (budget 2-5). Cliopatria has no Carinthia row. Not settled: the 976 extent (the page does not map Carinthia; Carniola is read in from the 1040 split), which marches stayed under the duke after 1040, the Carniolan margraves, why the Bavarian pages say Styria was separated from Bavaria in 1180 although the March of Styria page puts it under Carinthia from 976 (the Bavaria dossier leaves Styria out), the Sponheim and later dukes 1122-1335, and Carinthia's southern edge (Friuli, Gorizia). No complete list of dukes is on the page, so no ruler strip. The Verona page's 1061 enfeoffment of Berthold with Carinthia and Verona is not given its own event. Counterparts needing dossiers: march-of-styria, march-of-verona (both in this batch), March of Carniola, March of Istria.
